source.title: Over-parameterization as a Catalyst for Better Generalization of Deep ReLU network

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper and supplementary material. The title in the text is “Student Specialization in Deep Rectified Networks With Finite Width and Input Dimension,” which differs from the catalog title.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains over-realized ReLU students on labels generated by fixed teacher networks and measures specialization and evaluation performance; this is a conceptual test of how over-realization relates to generalization, though it does not test the mapped natural-label/random-label claim directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports teacher-student regression and CIFAR-10 classification results. It does not test random-label memorization, held-out generalization on natural labels under the same recipe, or most optimizer, batch-size, regularization, and sharpness claims. Rows below cover its reported evaluation-loss or accuracy results and over-realization comparisons. The paper’s many specialization-correlation plots are not separate rows because they measure alignment, not a named version’s generalization gap.
record.test_reason: The study measures teacher–student specialization and held-out performance, but does not establish widening beyond a width that achieves zero training error. Its CIFAR-10 width comparison therefore does not test V2's defining condition. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The theoretical result is conditional: under dataset, teacher, observation, and small per-sample-gradient assumptions, teacher nodes have aligned student nodes at the lowest layer. It does not prove SGD reaches these conditions. Experiments show specialization, improved CIFAR-10 evaluation accuracy with greater over-realization, and lower evaluation loss with teacher-aware data.
record.recipe_differences: Teacher-student learning from fixed teacher outputs rather than natural-label training; the study measures node specialization and evaluation loss or accuracy, not random-label memorization or the specified width sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation loss varies with teacher-aware versus teacher-agnostic data; CIFAR-10 evaluation accuracy varies with over-realization (1×, 2×, 5×).

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 average/maximum evaluation accuracy increases from 79.67% / 80.15% at 1× to 83.09% / 83.48% at 2× and 83.85% / 84.18% at 5× teacher-relative width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing student width relative to a pruned teacher improves held-out accuracy in this teacher–student experiment, without establishing a post-interpolation regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher-aware data yields substantially lower evaluation loss than teacher-agnostic data despite low training loss in both cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher-dependent data construction can improve generalization in synthetic teacher–student learning.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed 2× student width, increasing sample count improves generalization and teacher–student activation correlation under MSE and cross-entropy losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More training samples improve held-out performance and specialization in these synthetic teacher–student networks.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The teacher-student setup does not directly establish natural-label generalization after random-label memorization. Several evaluation-loss results are shown only in figures without numeric values in the supplied text; reported CIFAR-10 accuracy has no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Node specialization and recovery-rate plots (Figures 5–8) are left out because correlation and matching rates do not measure the generalization gap or held-out error named by the versions. Figure 10's layerwise correlation curves are likewise not separate generalization results.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
Held-out error as width increases beyond an empirically established zero-training-error threshold; neither that threshold nor a post-threshold error trend is established.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons with fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to the training recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V2 verdicts. A width-related accuracy improvement without an established interpolation threshold is insufficient for support; a different experimental setting or an untested component is also insufficient for limits_scope. States marked cannot_determine concern the named versions, not whether the reported auxiliary findings occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes.

The stated one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, and test error beyond the interpolation threshold. This paper uses teacher-student networks and reports evaluation performance, not the specified setting.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.
